single_change: Halve the learning-rate multiplier from 2 to 1; retain the exact centering architecture, fixed 50-update warmup and all other optimizer settings.
motivation: The user asked whether the learning rate explains the slower centering results. Its first twelve LR x2 screen cells pass but small-prime division and recall regress. This separate sensitivity experiment distinguishes a rate-specific result from evidence across two rates; it cannot prove optimality.
hypothesis: Mean subtraction followed by RMS can change gradient magnitudes and conditioning; a smaller update may improve learning. This remains a hypothesis, not a mathematical guarantee.
screen_policy: Keep original budgets. Require 18/18 passes and improvement in at least three of the six per-task median paired epoch ratios versus LR x2 to advance. Preserve every screen row. No screen-only aggregate geometric mean is reported.
parent_comparison: Retain all paired cells against both the LR x2 centering parent and the scaled Peri-RMS model without centering. Promotion still uses the same LR x2 control.
full_suite_policy: Evaluate all 75 paired short cells for every candidate that advances. Prefer complete coverage, then lower full-suite geometric-mean epochs. Compare against both original baseline and LR x2; include all per-task medians/worst cases, slower seeds and censoring. If no candidate improves on LR x2, retain the incumbent and report the negative results.
long_policy: Include this LR sensitivity screen, and its full short suite if promoted, before final short-only selection. Run the final new winner once on the already observed long diagnostic; do not tune or reselect from long.
invariants: Unchanged frozen model sources, task manifest, data, seeds, batch order, dimensions, dtype, warmup, weight decay, evaluation cadence and update budgets; separately archived code/configuration for every new output directory.
execution_order: Finish the current LR x2 centering screen, validate the LR x1 captured update, then run the LR x1 centering screen. All configurations retain their own source plan and output directory.
